primary_claim: MonitoringBench, a dataset of human-seeded and agentically-refined AI-control attack trajectories, shows that monitoring capability declines steeply for weaker models (Opus-4.5 achieves 71% caught-attack/safety rate on the HARD dataset vs 11% for GPT-5 and 0% for GPT-5-nano), that naive Opus-4.5-elicited red-teaming suffers severe mode collapse (92% of attacks fall into the easiest technical category), and that the benchmark's human-seed-plus-refinement red-teaming pipeline can reduce an Opus-4.5 monitor's safety score by 21%.

effect.metric: monitor safety score / caught-attack rate (%) on MonitoringBench HARD and EASY datasets
effect.value: HARD dataset: Opus-4.5 71% safety, GPT-5 11%, GPT-5-nano 0%; EASY dataset: Opus-4.5 92.6% caught-attack rate; human-seed + refinement red-teaming reduces Opus-4.5 monitor's safety score by 21% relative to unassisted elicitation

contradicts_or_qualifies: Argues current red-teaming approaches (Bhatt et al. 2025, Loughridge et al. 2025, Terekhov et al. 2025) systematically under-elicit attacks due to mode collapse, a conceive-execute gap, and hard/brittle elicitation, motivating MonitoringBench's human-seeded-plus-refinement approach as a stronger alternative.
stated_future_work: Expand to more side tasks in BashArena beyond the firewall task
Scale the refinement pipeline to be more automated
Run mini-evals with matched trajectory pairs to isolate specific monitor skills and failure modes (e.g. task-drift distraction, connecting distant suspicious actions)
limitations_stated: Current agents cannot reliably execute sophisticated attack strategies in real time, so the refinement pipeline simulates a more capable attacker via post-hoc edits rather than reflecting genuine zero-shot agent capability
Varying the monitor prompt on the HARD dataset gave non-robust improvements: prompt changes that help one monitor model can hurt another, and results vary substantially across models and runs
Coverage is currently limited to a single side task (firewall/IP whitelisting) on the BashArena environment

LLM attacker capability does not scale as cleanly with general model capability as monitor capability does, making attacker capability trends harder to establish (frontier models may be more safety-tuned than predecessors)
quote: Monitoring capability declines steeply for weaker models, e.g. Opus-4.5 achieves 71% safety (as caught attack rate), GPT-5 11% and GPT-5-nano 0% on our HARD dataset.
